result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A leaves the claim window, remedy and coverage as visible placeholders with example options, and adds a scoped exclusions line. It also gives a short version for near the Book Now button and makes every trust line conditional on being true. Answer B is more persuasive copy, but it writes invented terms into the published text as if they were settled: the 30-day and 1-year windows, payment for damage, no deposit and a photo or hose test on every job. It only flags these as suggestions in the notes below, and it leaves the fine print out of the copy itself. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Answer B covers every part of the guarantee (window, how to claim, remedy, what's covered and what isn't) and uses visible placeholders for everything the brief didn't give. It also adds a short version to place near the Book Now button. Answer A reads more persuasively, but it bakes invented terms into the copy (30 days, 1 year, no deposit, photo or hose test) and only flags them in the notes after the draft. It also leaves out how a homeowner actually makes a claim.
